For the transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3,$ defined as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/bbb9192192b4d73f4993b3131a2b0bb1d0a0cddb77b754940d1b7684bfb08336.svg)

the total derivative $\boldsymbol f'$ is given by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/2cf231879630af578e33b201e5be0f65d019da9c49da7789f5921c05a8249c09.svg)
From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?
question.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/49c118b037a1589c6feb2c96afeaccb15fe905663393800638baff8cef327a3a.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/a5ed3766e8ed6a2a5fd249078e244dfab19b1c20d55548c27a7053bd0130c278.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/23d7804912a10685756bb4ec89d12e3f6659b435ebe4d22c436684fb6eef9df8.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})=2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{y}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/eae5dd91db0cc17bec3af0a4781c7a58e8c65edb6c4139642f9c806dfc9c2473.svg)
Thus, the missing entries are $y,\:$ $0,\:$ and $\ln{x}.$
